parts.note: a jack is a device for lifting a car or other heavy load
kite is old RAF slang for an aircraft, so it stands for plane

explanation.surface: Someone describes a gentler way of getting a kite up into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: A JACK PLANE is a carpenter's tool for smoothing wood; 'kite' is old flying slang for an aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: This carpenter's plane is used to level and smooth timber, so it is a smoother.

clue.text: His ladder used by poor chap (with bill enclosed)

indicators.note: with a bill enclosed means the word for bill goes inside the word for the poor chap

parts.note: Job is the long-suffering man of the Old Testament, the classic poor chap
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A ladder belonging to someone is being used by a hard-up man carrying an invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis the patriarch dreams of a ladder reaching to heaven, so 'His ladder' points to its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical dream of a stairway to heaven belongs to this patriarch, the son of Isaac.

indicators.note: a trick played on these letters plays them false, jumbling the order

explanation.surface: Someone holds a licence to perform the find-the-lady card con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three-card trick' reads as the con game, but 'trick' rearranges THREE and CARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A chartered body or accountant holds an official licence or royal charter to operate.

parts.note: to ponder is to think something over, so contemplates gives ponders
a terminal point is an end

explanation.surface: Someone muses about a station close to a north London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: PONDERS END is a district of the London Borough of Enfield, on the city's northern edge.
explanation.definitionFit: This district lies in north London beside the town centre of Enfield, so it is located near there.

clue.text: Deficiency said to increase cardiac weakness

explanation.surface: A shortage is reported to make the heart weaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'absence makes the heart grow fonder': growing fond is the heart's weakness.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack of something is its absence; the saying claims being apart makes a heart grow fonder.

indicators.note: trading swaps things about, so these letters are exchanged into a new order

explanation.surface: A Greek town makes its money from dealing in livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trading' rearranges US and SHEEP. Ephesus was an ancient Greek city in Ionia, now in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a major ancient Greek city on the Ionian coast, a centre of trade and worship.

parts.note: the fifth letter of the composer's name is H, and this is that letter spelt out in full

explanation.surface: A request to play the whole of a famous symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's fifth' suggests the symphony, but it is the fifth letter, H, written as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter H, fifth in the composer's name, is written as a word with five letters.

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for star is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly flares in brightness

explanation.surface: A local celebrity is on the way up in the shire.
explanation.walkthrough: AVON was an English county around Bristol and Bath, 1974 to 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the name of a former administrative county in the west of England.

clue.text: What is struck by Barking people, say?

definitions.text: What is struck by Barking people, say?

parts.words: What is struck by Barking people, say?
parts.note: to bark one's shin is to knock it painfully, and this is the shin bone that gets knocked

explanation.surface: Asking what the residents of Barking, a London district, hit.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is an east London district, but here barking means scraping the skin off your shin.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the shin bone, the one people scrape when they bark a shin against furniture.

clue.text: Delirious on heroin? Arrogant type is on it

parts.note: someone delirious with joy or drugs is high
horse is drug slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug user gets wildly elated, and the snooty person is also on something.
explanation.walkthrough: An arrogant person is said to be 'on their high horse'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's high horse is an idiom for behaving with haughty superiority.

indicators.note: about means the word for the feature wraps around the letter a

parts.note: the chin is the facial feature a boxer leads with

explanation.surface: A headline story concerning a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading feature' suggests a newspaper article; it is the chin, since a careless fighter 'leads with the chin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of linked rings forms a joining, so a union of things is a linkage.

parts.note: reads as an argument in favour of state secondaries, but means a satchel pupils carry

explanation.surface: Someone argues in favour of comprehensive education.
explanation.walkthrough: Comprehensives are British state secondary schools; 'case' is a bag, not an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is the case in which pupils carry books to lessons.

clue.text: Resentment some show, having head on beer?

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows after it

parts.note: bitter is a type of British beer
a ness is a headland, a head of land

explanation.surface: Some folk show bad feeling when their pint arrives with a froth on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head on beer' suggests froth; NESS is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitterness is lingering ill feeling, the same as resentment.

explanation.surface: A request for a laundry room.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a large bay on the east coast of England, between Norfolk and Lincolnshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry waiting to be cleaned is the washing; the second sense is the named East Anglian inlet.

parts.note: Sir Christopher Cockerell invented the vessel that rides on a cushion of air

explanation.surface: An infant is handed an inflatable cushion.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Cockerell, a British engineer, invented the air-cushion vehicle in the 1950s, his 'baby'.
explanation.definitionFit: This craft travels supported on a cushion of air, Cockerell's invention.

explanation.surface: Expecting things is a godlike gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' reads as an adjective but is the verb, to predict.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate events is to predict them; to divine is likewise to prophesy what will happen.

clue.text: Clear change of direction leads to coast

parts.note: free means clear, as in clear of obstruction
a wheel is a turning movement, as soldiers wheel left

explanation.surface: A clean shift of route takes you down to the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coast' looks like the seaside but is the verb: to roll along without pedalling.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride a bike without pedalling, rolling on momentum, is to coast.

parts.note: reads as the name of a town, but means an obstruction that blocks players potting balls

explanation.surface: Naming an example of a town in Hertfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Potters Bar is a town just north of London; in this game players 'pot' balls and a blocked shot is barred.
explanation.definitionFit: In this cue game a player is barred from a direct shot by an obstructing ball.

parts.note: the sharp side of a blade matters to a cutler, and the phrase also means a precarious moment

explanation.surface: Asking about a crisis in a cutlery maker's life.
explanation.walkthrough: A cutler makes and sells blades; being on this is to be in a precarious state.
explanation.definitionFit: To be balanced on a blade's sharp side is an idiom for a tense, critical situation.

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Decisions made while looking after a flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolutions' here means the ways stories are wound up.
explanation.definitionFit: The resolutions of stories are their conclusions, the way plots finish.

clue.text: Up with the lark, signora is agitated

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters of the Italian title are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: An Italian lady rises early, and she is in a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up with the lark' suggests rising early, but means flying high like the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark climbs high when it sings, so climbing up alongside it is flying high.

clue.text: Lister worked with energy to be so germ-free

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Joseph Lister laboured with vigour to make surgery germ-free.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery, which fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sterile has no living microbes, so it is free of germs.

explanation.surface: A churchman alongside a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' reads as the churchman; it is the adjective meaning chief or paramount.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean highest in rank: cardinal as principal, sovereign as holding ultimate power.

parts.note: W is an abbreviation for woman or wife
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A mistress treated poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy woman' reads as a mistress; 'Fancy' is the verb, to wish for.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to want it, and to will it is to desire it.

parts.note: describes a beam of light concentrated to an intense focus

explanation.surface: Gossip that someone named Ray is focusing hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name but is a beam of light, concentrated intensely in this device.
explanation.definitionFit: This device produces an intense, concentrated beam of light, a focused ray.

parts.note: bread is slang for money, so these are the envelopes holding wages

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money; these envelopes hold a worker's wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Envelopes holding weekly wages wrap up the money, and bread is slang for cash.

parts.note: reads as a rest for medics, but means an air-filled cavity in the skull named in anatomy

explanation.surface: Asking for a break for overworked medics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathing-space' suggests a rest; it is an air cavity in the skull, as a doctor would name it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an air-filled cavity in the bones of the face, part of the breathing passages.

parts.note: South and West are two of the four players at bridge, abbreviated S and W
ay is an old word for always, also spelt aye

explanation.surface: Card players who are permanently in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge partnerships are named by compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold sway is to have power or rule, so sway is control.

indicators.note: broken up means smashed into pieces, so these letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A former Welsh ceremony was disrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: Erstwhile means former, of an earlier time.

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat

explanation.surface: Asking whether a poet is a subject for academic research.
explanation.walkthrough: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American poet.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was a major 20th-century poet, so the clue's poet is him.

clue.text: One road-vehicle left as alternative to rail

parts.note: or is the word that offers an alternative
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A truck is picked instead of the train for freight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One road-vehicle' is a single truck.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large goods truck, a type of road vehicle in British English.

indicators.note: mess means a muddle, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A famous figure dining among the sergeants in the military mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' reads as the army dining hall but is the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity is fame, eminence, and so greatness of standing.
